guide_enrichment.narrative:
Wake Forest’s opener supplies an obvious reason for market optimism: it produced 559 yards, while Gio Lopez threw for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. We are not dismissing that performance, but we are also not treating one game against Akron as proof of a new baseline. Purdue produced 523 yards of its own, with Ryan Browne throwing for 317 yards and three scores. For us, those openers provide context without creating enough separation to justify making Purdue a clear home underdog.

The more interesting part is Purdue’s defensive path. It held Indiana State to 284 total yards and 66 on the ground while generating eight tackles for loss and three sacks. Wake Forest allowed no sacks in its opener, so Purdue’s pressure will face a more meaningful test. Still, our position does not require Purdue to control every phase; we think its defense gives it a credible chance to keep the game within a narrow margin while the market is asking Wake Forest to create separation.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are focused on Purdue’s passing offense against Wake Forest’s pass defense. Our matchup data gives Wake Forest a substantial advantage in this phase, which is the clearest concern for our Purdue position. Browne’s efficient opener and Purdue’s 11 players with a reception showed useful distribution, but the question is whether that production holds up against a defense our numbers rate much more highly. Purdue does not need to dominate this matchup for our wager to work, but it cannot allow Wake Forest’s coverage advantage to dictate the game.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 victory over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 203 rushing yards and 356 passing yards.
Wake Forest allowed Akron 305 total yards, including 149 rushing and 156 passing.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers and recovered one Akron fumble in the opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue opened its season with a 44-19 victory over Indiana State on Sept. 4.
Purdue generated 523 total yards against Indiana State, including 346 passing yards and 177 rushing yards.
Purdue converted all six of its red-zone opportunities against Indiana State.
Eleven Purdue receivers caught at least one pass against Indiana State.
Asaad Waseem led Purdue with 107 receiving yards and a touchdown on six catches, while Xavier Townsend had a team-high seven catches for 47 yards.
Fame Ijeboi led Purdue's rushing attack with 87 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, averaging 7.9 yards per attempt.
Purdue held Indiana State to 284 total yards and 66 rushing yards while recording eight tackles for loss and three sacks.
Purdue defensive back Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss and one sack against Indiana State.
Purdue senior Don Saunders recorded the defense's lone turnover against Indiana State with his sixth career interception.

quarterback.fact: Wake Forest starter Gio Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions in his Demon Deacon debut against Akron; he also rushed for 39 yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of Lopez's collegiate career.
Lopez transferred to Wake Forest from North Carolina in January 2026 after previously playing at South Alabama under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell.
Across 28 career games and 24 starts, Lopez has completed 65.8 percent of his passes for 5,131 yards, 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, while rushing for 791 yards and 12 touchdowns.
Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions against Indiana State.

offensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's projected offensive line lists Tolu Olajide at left tackle, Clinton Richard at left guard, Will Way at center, Ryan Berger at right guard and Aidan Martin at right tackle.
Projected starting center Will Way transferred from Weber State in January 2026 and was selected as a team captain.
Ty Clark III rushed for a career-high 105 yards on seven carries against Akron, including a career-long 57-yard run.
Carlos Hernandez caught five passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against Akron and finished with 183 all-purpose yards.
Hernandez has averaged 107.6 receiving yards over Wake Forest's last five games, with at least five catches in every game and five total touchdowns during that span.
Antonio Meeks recorded 93 receiving yards against Akron.

defensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's projected defensive front consists of ends Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke, tackle Dallas Afalava and nose guard Zach Lohavichan.
Wake Forest's projected linebackers are Frank Cusano and Aiden Hall, with Braylon Johnson at the Star position.
Wake Forest's projected secondary lists Deuce Blades II and Ashaad Williams at cornerback, Rushaun Tongue at free safety and Davaughn Patterson at strong safety.
Aiden Hall became a starter in 2025 and finished that season with 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defensed.
Braylon Johnson recorded one of Wake Forest's two sacks against Akron.

coaching_changes.fact: Jake Dickert is in his second season as Wake Forest's head coach after being hired on Dec. 18, 2024; his Wake Forest record is 10-4.
Dyrell Roberts joined Wake Forest as wide receivers coach for the 2026 season after coaching East Carolina's wide receivers from 2023 through 2025.

Rob Ezell serves as Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, Dan Enos as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, Scottie Hazelton as defensive coordinator and Freddie Banks as co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.

special_teams.fact: Wake Forest kicker Connor Calvert made three field goals and scored 12 points against Akron.

recent_game.fact: Purdue opened the 2026 season with a 44-19 home victory over Indiana State.
Purdue produced 523 yards of total offense against Indiana State, its first 500-yard game since Oct. 12, 2024.
Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana State.
Fame Ijeboi led Purdue with 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries in his debut.
FAU transfer Asaad Waseem caught six passes for 107 yards and one touchdown in his Purdue debut.
Don Saunders returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown, Purdue's first pick-six since 2022.
Purdue allowed Indiana State 284 total yards, including 66 rushing yards, and recorded three sacks.
Sixteen players made their first starts as Boilermakers in the season opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue hosts Wake Forest at Ross-Ade Stadium on Sept. 12; both teams enter the game 1-0.
This will be Purdue's ninth game against an ACC opponent this century.

quarterback.fact: Ryan Browne is Purdue's returning starting quarterback and has started 15 career games for the Boilermakers.
Browne started all 12 games in 2025 and passed for 2,153 yards and nine touchdowns.
Browne's 317-yard opener was his fourth career 300-yard passing game.
Browne returned to Purdue through the spring transfer window in 2025 after spending that spring at North Carolina.
Evans Chuba and Bennett Meredith competed during the spring and summer for the backup quarterback role; Meredith previously started against Northwestern in 2023 but has not played in two seasons.

offensive_personnel.fact: Brock Brownfield became Purdue's first true freshman offensive lineman to start a season opener since freshmen became eligible in 1972.
Joey Tanona is the only returning offensive lineman who started all 12 games in 2025; Ethan Trent made six starts and Jude McCoskey played in 11 games.
Purdue added five offensive-line transfers, including Boaz Stanley with 21 previous starts, Nuku Mafi with 12 and Micah Banuelos with five.
The running back room changed after Devin Mockobee graduated; Antonio Harris is the only returning running back after rushing for 305 yards and two touchdowns in 2025.
Minnesota transfer Fame Ijeboi entered Purdue after rushing for 441 yards in 2025 and led the Boilermakers' backfield in the 2026 opener.
Xavier Townsend made his Purdue debut with seven catches for 47 yards and three punt returns for 24 yards.
Wide receivers De'Nylon Morrissette and Chauncey Magwood returned after missing the 2025 season with injuries.
Magwood caught a six-yard touchdown against Indiana State, his first touchdown since 2022.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Charles Correa returned after starting all 12 games in 2025 and recording 96 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks.
FIU transfer Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass breakup against Indiana State.
Utah transfer Don Saunders made his Purdue debut with three tackles, a half-tackle for loss and a 35-yard interception return for a touchdown.
Illinois transfer Jojo Hayden started his Purdue debut and made four tackles with one tackle for loss.
Purdue added defensive linemen Rodney Lora, Curt Neal and Wisdom Simms, who brought a combined 81 games of college experience, including 60 at the Power Four level.
Ian Jeffries recorded three tackles and one sack against Indiana State after playing all 12 games with six starts in 2025.
New defensive backs Jaden Mangham, Don Saunders and John Slaughter were among Purdue's first-time starters in the opener.

coaching_changes.fact: Kevin Kane returned to Purdue as defensive coordinator and linebackers coach after serving as a Minnesota defensive analyst in 2025; he previously coordinated Purdue's defense in 2023 and 2024.
Zach Crabtree is Purdue's new offensive line coach after holding the same position at Fresno State in 2025.
Cornell Ford moved from wide receivers coach to running backs coach for 2026.
Bilal Marshall was promoted from offensive analyst to wide receivers coach during the offseason.
Charles Clark joined Purdue as defensive pass game coordinator and defensive backs coach after five seasons at Memphis.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Kylan Fox suffered an injury at the start of training camp and is expected to miss the season.
Tight end George Burhenn returned against Indiana State for his first game action in 349 days and caught two passes for 43 yards.
Wide receiver Chauncey Magwood returned after missing most of the 2025 season with an injury and caught a touchdown in the opener.

offensive_context.fact: Purdue's opener featured three passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown on offense.
Browne completed 79.3 percent of his passes and averaged 10.9 yards per attempt against Indiana State.
Ijeboi averaged 7.9 yards per carry and added two receptions for 30 yards in the opener.
Waseem became the first Purdue player since Charlie Jones in 2022 to exceed 100 receiving yards in his Boilermaker debut.

defensive_context.fact: Purdue limited Indiana State to 12 first downs in the season opener.
Purdue recorded eight tackles for loss and three sacks against Indiana State.
The Boilermakers won the turnover margin in the opener without committing a turnover.

special_teams.fact: True freshman kicker Jacobo Echeverria Lozano made all three field-goal attempts and all five extra points against Indiana State.
Echeverria Lozano's three field goals were the most by a Purdue freshman in a game since at least 1995.
Buffalo transfer Dylan Drennan punted once for 54 yards with a net of 49 yards in his Purdue debut.
Xavier Townsend returned three punts for 24 yards against Indiana State.

series_context.fact: Purdue leads the all-time series against Wake Forest 4-1, including a 3-1 record in West Lafayette.
This is the sixth Purdue-Wake Forest meeting and the first since Purdue won 16-10 at Wake Forest on Sept. 13, 2003.

other_relevant.fact: Purdue added 32 transfers and 22 freshmen during the 2026 offseason, including 19 transfers from Power Four programs.
Thirty-eight players appeared in their first game for Purdue during the season-opening victory.
